title: Affinity-label fragmentation: autoscaler misconfig root-cause diary
body:
Summary:

This is a running diary and salvage plan for the late-Oct/Nov incident where Dedicated GPU pool throughput and tail latency degraded over multiple days despite nominal node counts. The immediate symptoms were a persistent p95/p99 token-latency increase on the 'dedicated-gamma' pools, increased evictions, and a steady decline in effective tenant packing density (slots utilized / slots provisioned).

Why this doc exists (goal):
- capture the step-by-step sleuthing we did during nightshifts
- document the root cause hypothesis and evidence chain
- propose short-term mitigations and long-term config/runbook changes
- list concrete follow-ups (owners + tickets) so this doesn't reoccur

High-level hypothesis (short):
Autoscaler label defaulting + a recent flag change caused affinity labels to be applied to a subset of newly provisioned nodes. That produced logical fragmentation: tenants with 'preferred-affinity=true' got placed on a shrinking subset of nodes, while remaining nodes were treated as incompatible for those tenants. Autoscaler scaling decisions and bin-packing heuristics did not detect the fragmentation, so we ended up with under-packed nodes (lots of low-util machines) and hotspots (few nodes with many hot tenants) which amplified noisy-neighbor effects and pushed queueing/evictions.

Timeline (key entries):
- 2024-11-02 22:13 PST: First pager (~p95 increase) from production alerting; oncall rotated to Diego.
- 2024-11-02 23:05 PST: Observed sustained p99 latency elevation + small increase in eviction_rate.
- 2024-11-03 01:40 PST: Attempted immediate mitigation: scaled pool up (+20%) to buy breathing room; short-term tail improved but p99 still high.
- 2024-11-03 04:10 PST: Noticed imbalance in tenant distribution: ~38% of tenants pinned to 12% of nodes in gamma pool (query below).
- 2024-11-03 07:20 PST: Correlated with deploy (2024-11-01) of autoscaler v2.3.4 which introduced a default label insertion for 'preferred-affinity'.
- 2024-11-03 10:30 PST: Hotfix: revert label defaulting in autoscaler config and trigger a controlled node replacement.
- 2024-11-03 16:00 PST: Observed gradual improvement after rolling drainage and reallocation; full stabilization by 2024-11-04.

Signals & queries used (examples):
- PromQL to measure packing density per node: 
  sum by(node) (dedicated_allocated_tenants{pool="gamma"}) / sum by(node) (max_tenants_per_node)
- Node-level entropy check (quick heuristic):
  topk(20, sum by(node, tenant_id) (rate(requests_total[5m])))
- SQL we used to find tenant placement skew (prod_placements.placements table):
  SELECT node_id, count(tenant_id) AS tenant_count FROM placements WHERE pool='gamma' AND created_at > '2024-11-01' GROUP BY node_id ORDER BY tenant_count DESC LIMIT 200;

Immediate investigative steps run during oncall: (raw log of commands + notes)
- kubectl get nodes -l pool=gamma -o wide  # confirmed nodes had "affinity=preferred-true" label set on subset
- kubectl describe node <node-xyz>  # saw kubelet annotations added by autoscaler
- curl -s "https://api.internal/placements?node=<node-xyz>&since=2024-11-01" | jq '. | length'  # number of placements - anomalously high for 3 nodes
- ran small synthetic tenant hammer (1k seq tokens) against low-populated node -> low latency as expected
- re-ran same hammer against hot nodes -> severe queuing, token-per-second flatline

Why autoscaler misconfigured (detailed):
- v2.3.4 autoscaler change introduced an opt-out label setting: if a node config lacks explicit label, autoscaler will set label 'preferred-affinity=true' by default to prefer older families for certain customers. The rollout was asymmetric: only new nodes created after 2024-11-01 had the label inserted.
- The placement service uses label matching as a soft constraint for tenant assignment. Tenants with legacy affinity flags were updated in a recent migration (PR: infrastructure/placement/PR-834) to prefer nodes with that label. The combination produced a meta-group of tenants that the placement service attempted to cluster onto labeled nodes.
- The autoscaler does not currently have a fragmentation-awareness metric: it looks at pool-level free_slots and p95 latency for scaling decisions. Because raw free slots were present across the pool, scaler did not see a need to repack.

Evidence chain (bulletproofing our root cause):
- Correlation between label-first-appearance time and tenant skew in placements table (see SQL); timestamps line up within the deploy window.
- Nodes with label consumed >3x average tenant connections and showed higher kernel scheduling stalls (dmesg excerpts attached to JIRA).
- After removing the label on a small subset and rebalancing, packing density normalized within two allocation waves and p99 dropped ~35%.

Short-term mitigations executed and rationale: 
1) Reverted autoscaler label default in config and cut a small hotfix (infrastructure PR 912). Rationale: stop adding new fragmentation source.
2) Controlled drain+replace of the top-12% hottest nodes (drain -> cordon -> reprovision) to force the placement service to distribute tenants across all nodes. Rationale: induce a re-pack without a global migration.
3) Increased autoscaler observation window for p95 -> 10m to avoid over-reacting to short noise spikes; added a temporary hysteresis to avoid frequent oscillation.

Runbook steps (proposed edits) — quick playbook for any future similar event: 
- Pager: p95 > 2x baseline for > 10min OR packing_density < 0.5 for > 15min -> level2 oncall + eng-sre pager.
- Triage checklist (first 30 minutes):
  * check placement skew: run SQL from Signals section
  * check node labels: kubectl get nodes -L preferred-affinity
  * check autoscaler config change history: git log on infra/auto-configs
  * if fragmentation present, escalate to eng-placement and autoscaler owners
- Manual fix steps (if fragmentation confirmed):
  * temporarily stop autoscaler new node creation for affected pool (toggle flag in config)
  * pick 5-12 hottest nodes and cordon/drain them with placement-safe-drain script
  * monitor packing_density and p99 after each 2 node replacement cycles
  * only resume normal scaling after packing_density > 0.8 and p99 back to baseline for 60m

Longer-term changes recommended (engineering):
- Add a fragmentation metric to autoscaler input: e.g., variance(tenants_per_node) or Gini coefficient over tenant counts per node. Use as signal to trigger repack/scale actions.
- Make the autoscaler label behavior explicit and require a config opt-in for default labels (no silent defaults).
- Modify placement service to treat 'preferred-affinity' as a soft preference weighted against packing cost; include a packing penalty if preference would reduce global packing density below threshold.
- Introduce a synthetic nightly "packing smoke" test that provisions 100 synthetic tenants across gamma-like pools and validates packing_density and p99. Failures create an alert to eng-sre.

Follow-ups / action items (owner — ticket — due):
- Diego: create JIRA to track fragmentation-aware autoscaler metric (SRE-1499) — due 2024-11-22
- Priya: PR to remove defaulting behavior from autoscaler and add explicit opt-in flag (infra/auto-configs) — PR opened (github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/912) — merge + rollout by 2024-11-18
- Evan: improve placement scoring to cash in packing penalty and add unit tests (placement service) — JIRA PLAC-233 — due 2025-01-10
- Samira: add 'packing smoke' nightly job and alert integration in grafana — due 2024-12-01

Notes to self / raw observations (freeform):
- The incident felt deeply stealthy because node counts looked fine; this is a classic logical fragmentation vs physical capacity problem.
- We should consider making packing_density a first-class SLO for Dedicated pools (rolling 1h window).
- Oncalls found value in the SQL placement table — need to make a simple dashboard that surfaces the top-20 busiest nodes and a skew metric.

Attachments & references (internal):
- linked artifacts (above) + dmesg snippets and sample placement query outputs attached to JIRA SRE-1427.
- timeline slack threads: #sre-incidents thread (links in JIRA)

End of diary.

(If you're reading this during triage: start with the triage checklist in the Runbook steps, then run the packing_density SQL. If packing density is low, follow Manual fix steps and loop in placement/autoscaler owners.)
